# zggev

> Compute the generalized eigenvalues and optionally the left and/or.

<section class="intro">

right generalized eigenvectors of a complex matrix pair (A, B).

When `work` (resp. `rwork`) is `null`, this LAPACKE-style wrapper allocates a
workspace as a convenience: `work` of the optimal size `N + N*NB + TSIZE`
complex elements and `rwork` of size `max(1,8*N)` real elements. Prefer
passing caller-owned buffers for batched use.

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zggev from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zggev';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zggev(
    order,
    jobvl, jobvr,
    N,
    A, LDA,
    B, LDB,
    ALPHA, strideALPHA,
    BETA, strideBETA,
    VL, LDVL,
    VR, LDVR,
    work,
    rwork
) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `jobvl` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | `'no-vectors'` or `'compute-vectors'` |
| `jobvr` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | `'no-vectors'` or `'compute-vectors'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of matrices A and B<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `B` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `B`<br>Requires `LDB ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `ALPHA` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output eigenvalue numerators |
| ↳ `strideALPHA` | `integer` | `ALPHA` stride length |
| `BETA` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output eigenvalue denominators |
| ↳ `strideBETA` | `integer` | `BETA` stride length |
| `VL` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Left eigenvector matrix |
| ↳ `LDVL` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `VL`<br>Rejects `ldvl < 1 \|\| ((jobvl === 'compute-vectors') && ldvl < N)` |
| `VR` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Right eigenvector matrix |
| ↳ `LDVR` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `VR`<br>Rejects `ldvr < 1 \|\| ((jobvr === 'compute-vectors') && ldvr < N)` |
| `work` | `Complex128Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, 2 * N)</sub> | **out** · Complex workspace of length at least `max(1,2*N)`; for optimal performance at least `N + N*NB + TSIZE` (`NB` from `ilaenv`, `TSIZE = 4160`), the reference's `N + N*NB` with the zunmqr optimum's T part, which enables the blocked QR steps; or `null` to allocate the optimal size<br>Optional, default `null`. |
| `rwork` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ 8 * N</sub> | **out** · Caller-provided real workspace (length >= max(1,8\*N)), or `null` to auto-allocate<br>Optional, default `null`. |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobvl`:

  -   `= 'N'`: do not compute the left generalized eigenvectors;
  -   `= 'V'`: compute the left generalized eigenvectors.
- `jobvr`:

  -   `= 'N'`: do not compute the right generalized eigenvectors;
  -   `= 'V'`: compute the right generalized eigenvectors.
- `N`: The order of the matrices A, B, `VL`, and `VR`. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the matrix A in the pair (A,B). On exit, A has been overwritten.
- `B`: On entry, the matrix B in the pair (A,B). On exit, B has been overwritten.
- `BETA`: On exit, `ALPHA(j)`/`BETA(j)`, $j=1$,...,N, will be the generalized eigenvalues.

  Note: the quotients `ALPHA(j)`/`BETA(j)` may easily over- or underflow, and `BETA(j)` may even be zero. Thus, the user should avoid naively computing the ratio $\alpha$/$\beta$. However, `ALPHA` will be always less than and usually comparable with norm(A) in magnitude, and `BETA` always less than and usually comparable with norm(B).
- `VL`: If `JOBVL = 'V'`, the left generalized eigenvectors u(j) are stored one after another in the columns of `VL`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. Each eigenvector is scaled so the largest component has abs(real part) + abs(imag. part) = 1. Not referenced if `JOBVL = 'N'`.
- `VR`: If `JOBVR = 'V'`, the right generalized eigenvectors v(j) are stored one after another in the columns of `VR`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. Each eigenvector is scaled so the largest component has abs(real part) + abs(imag. part) = 1. Not referenced if `JOBVR = 'N'`.
- `work`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` fourteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `LDVL < 1 \|\| ( ( jobvl === "compute-vectors" ) && LDVL < N )`)
- `RangeError` sixteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `LDVR < 1 \|\| ( ( jobvr === "compute-vectors" ) && LDVR < N )`)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zggev.ndarray(
    jobvl, jobvr,
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    ALPHA, strideALPHA, offsetALPHA,
    BETA, strideBETA, offsetBETA,
    VL, strideVL1, strideVL2, offsetVL,
    VR, strideVR1, strideVR2, offsetVR,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    RWORK, strideRWork, offsetRWork
) → integer
```

Compute the generalized eigenvalues and optionally the left and/or.
right generalized eigenvectors of a complex matrix pair (A, B).

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `jobvl` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | `'no-vectors'` or `'compute-vectors'` |
| `jobvr` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | `'no-vectors'` or `'compute-vectors'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of matrices A and B<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · First complex matrix (modified in-place) |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of A (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of A (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for A (complex elements) |
| `B` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Second complex matrix (modified in-place) |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of B (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of B (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for B (complex elements) |
| `ALPHA` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output eigenvalue numerators |
| ↳ `strideALPHA` | `integer` | Stride for ALPHA (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetALPHA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for ALPHA (complex elements) |
| `BETA` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output eigenvalue denominators |
| ↳ `strideBETA` | `integer` | Stride for BETA (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetBETA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for BETA (complex elements) |
| `VL` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Left eigenvector matrix |
| ↳ `strideVL1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of VL (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideVL2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of VL (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetVL` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for VL (complex elements) |
| `VR` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Right eigenvector matrix |
| ↳ `strideVR1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of VR (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideVR2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of VR (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetVR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for VR (complex elements) |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, 2 * N)</sub> | **out** · Complex workspace of length at least `max(1,2*N)`; for optimal performance at least `N + N*NB + TSIZE` (`NB` from `ilaenv`, `TSIZE = 4160`), the reference's `N + N*NB` with the zunmqr optimum's T part, which enables the blocked QR steps |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride for WORK (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for WORK (complex elements) |
| `RWORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ 8 * N</sub> | **out** · Caller-provided real workspace (length >= max(1,8\*N)) |
| ↳ `strideRWork` | `integer` | Stride for RWORK |
| ↳ `offsetRWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for RWORK |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobvl`:

  -   `= 'N'`: do not compute the left generalized eigenvectors;
  -   `= 'V'`: compute the left generalized eigenvectors.
- `jobvr`:

  -   `= 'N'`: do not compute the right generalized eigenvectors;
  -   `= 'V'`: compute the right generalized eigenvectors.
- `N`: The order of the matrices A, B, `VL`, and `VR`. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the matrix A in the pair (A,B). On exit, A has been overwritten.
- `B`: On entry, the matrix B in the pair (A,B). On exit, B has been overwritten.
- `BETA`: On exit, `ALPHA(j)`/`BETA(j)`, $j=1$,...,N, will be the generalized eigenvalues.

  Note: the quotients `ALPHA(j)`/`BETA(j)` may easily over- or underflow, and `BETA(j)` may even be zero. Thus, the user should avoid naively computing the ratio $\alpha$/$\beta$. However, `ALPHA` will be always less than and usually comparable with norm(A) in magnitude, and `BETA` always less than and usually comparable with norm(B).
- `VL`: If `JOBVL = 'V'`, the left generalized eigenvectors u(j) are stored one after another in the columns of `VL`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. Each eigenvector is scaled so the largest component has abs(real part) + abs(imag. part) = 1. Not referenced if `JOBVL = 'N'`.
- `VR`: If `JOBVR = 'V'`, the right generalized eigenvectors v(j) are stored one after another in the columns of `VR`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. Each eigenvector is scaled so the largest component has abs(real part) + abs(imag. part) = 1. Not referenced if `JOBVR = 'N'`.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

**Returns** `integer`: INFO: 0=success, 1..N=QZ iteration failed to converge, N+1=other QZ failure, N+2=ZTGEVC error

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` WORK array must have sufficient length
- `RangeError` RWORK array must have sufficient length

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.
-   `=1,...,N`:  The QZ iteration failed.  No eigenvectors have been calculated, but `ALPHA(j)` and `BETA(j)` should be correct for $j=\mathrm{INFO}+1$,...,N.
-   `> N`: =N+1: other then QZ iteration failed in ZHGEQZ, =N+2: error return from ZTGEVC.

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';
import zggev from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zggev';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
let A = new Complex128Array( discreteUniform( 2 * N * N, -10, 10, opts ) );
let B = new Complex128Array( discreteUniform( 2 * N * N, -10, 10, opts ) );
const VL = new Complex128Array( N * N );
const VR = new Complex128Array( N * N );
const ALPHA = new Complex128Array( N );
const BETA = new Complex128Array( N );

// Using the standard interface (internally allocated workspaces):
let out = zggev( 'column-major', 'compute-vectors', 'compute-vectors', N, A, N, B, N, ALPHA, 1, BETA, 1, VL, N, VR, N, null, null );
console.log( out, reinterpret( ALPHA, 0 ), reinterpret( BETA, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the ndarray interface (caller-provided workspaces):
A = new Complex128Array( discreteUniform( 2 * N * N, -10, 10, opts ) );
B = new Complex128Array( discreteUniform( 2 * N * N, -10, 10, opts ) );
const WORK = new Complex128Array( N + ( N * 32 ) + 4160 ); // the optimum; the minimum is 2*N
const RWORK = new Float64Array( 8 * N );
out = zggev.ndarray( 'compute-vectors', 'compute-vectors', N, A, 1, N, 0, B, 1, N, 0, ALPHA, 1, 0, BETA, 1, 0, VL, 1, N, 0, VR, 1, N, 0, WORK, 1, 0, RWORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( out, reinterpret( ALPHA, 0 ), reinterpret( BETA, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZGGEV`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZGGEV computes for a pair of N-by-N complex nonsymmetric matrices (A,B), the generalized eigenvalues, and optionally, the left and/or right generalized eigenvectors.

A generalized eigenvalue for a pair of matrices (A,B) is a scalar $\lambda$ or a ratio $\alpha /\beta = \lambda$, such that $A - \lambda \, B$ is singular. It is usually represented as the pair ($\alpha$,$\beta$), as there is a reasonable interpretation for $\beta =0$, and even for both being zero.

The right generalized eigenvector v(j) corresponding to the generalized eigenvalue lambda(j) of (A,B) satisfies

$$
A \, v(j) = \lambda (j) \, B \, v(j)
$$

The left generalized eigenvector u(j) corresponding to the generalized eigenvalues lambda(j) of (A,B) satisfies

$$
u(j)^H \, A = \lambda (j) \, u(j)^H \, B
$$

where $u(j)^H$ is the conjugate-transpose of u(j).

</section>
